name: Nielsen's 10 Usability Heuristics
author: Jakob Nielsen
description: The most widely used heuristic set for general interface evaluation.

heuristics.title: Visibility of System Status
heuristics.description: The design should always keep users informed about what is going on, through appropriate feedback within a reasonable amount of time.

heuristics.title: Match Between System and Real World
heuristics.description: The design should speak the users' language. Use words, phrases, and concepts familiar to the user, rather than internal jargon.

heuristics.title: User Control and Freedom
heuristics.description: Users often perform actions by mistake. They need a clearly marked 'emergency exit' to leave the unwanted action.

heuristics.title: Consistency and Standards
heuristics.description: Users should not have to wonder whether different words, situations, or actions mean the same thing.

heuristics.title: Error Prevention
heuristics.description: Good error messages are important, but the best designs carefully prevent problems from occurring in the first place.

heuristics.title: Recognition Rather Than Recall
heuristics.description: Minimize the user's memory load by making elements, actions, and options visible.

heuristics.title: Flexibility and Efficiency of Use
heuristics.description: Shortcuts — hidden from novice users — may speed up the interaction for the expert user.

heuristics.title: Aesthetic and Minimalist Design
heuristics.description: Interfaces should not contain information which is irrelevant or rarely needed.

heuristics.title: Help Users Recognize, Diagnose, and Recover from Errors
heuristics.description: Error messages should be expressed in plain language, precisely indicate the problem, and constructively suggest a solution.

heuristics.title: Help and Documentation
heuristics.description: It's best if the system doesn't need any additional explanation. However, it may be necessary to provide documentation.
